# Ligus

> Ligus is a local-first, end-to-end-encrypted desktop app for collaborating with AI agents. Workspaces and chats sync over an E2EE relay (or peer-to-peer); each device holds its own copy of the data and its own local code folder. Agents run on a host (your device or a headless worker), edit an isolated per-chat git worktree, and surface changes as reviewable proposals. The name is short for *ligustica* (Apis mellifera ligustica, the Italian honeybee); the project was called Hive until 2.0.

Documentation site: https://docs.ligus.ai/ — pages below are the canonical reference.

## Start here (for agents)

- [For agents: operating in Ligus](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/for-agents/): The operating rules an AI agent should assume — where you run and which files you can touch, that edits are reviewable proposals (not live changes), repo-relative-path rules, and how @mentions route work.

## Getting started

- [Install with Homebrew](https://docs.ligus.ai/getting-started/homebrew/): Installing the Ligus desktop app and CLI.
- [First launch](https://docs.ligus.ai/getting-started/first-launch/): First run, data directories, and resetting local data.
- [Configuring a runtime](https://docs.ligus.ai/getting-started/configuring-a-runtime/): Setting up LLM providers and CLI coding agents (claude, aider, pi, codex, Google Antigravity, GitHub Copilot).
- [Your first chat](https://docs.ligus.ai/getting-started/first-chat/): Sending a message and getting a first agent reply.

## Deploy

- [Choose a deployment](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/): The five deployment shapes (solo, personal fleet, team on a relay, Kubernetes preview, keys-off-cluster design) with architecture diagrams.
- [Solo laptop](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/solo/): The desktop app alone, no relay.
- [Personal fleet](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/personal-fleet/): Laptop plus an always-on `ligus serve` home server and the phone, directly over Tailscale or through the relay tunnel.
- [Team on a relay](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/deployment/): Deploying and gating a relay, creating a workspace, inviting teammates, a shared worker, and a security checklist.
- [Kubernetes (preview)](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/kubernetes/): The relay and ligus Helm charts (preview, unpublished), what each pod holds, and known limits.
- [Keys off the cluster (design)](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/keys-off-cluster/): A cluster that runs only the relay and executors; not shipped.
- [Multi-tenant (design)](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/multi-tenant/): Three authorization layers for hosting many organisations; not implemented.
- [Upgrading from Hive 1.x](https://docs.ligus.ai/deploy/upgrade-from-hive/): Env var rename, data migration per component, and rollback.

## Security

- [Security model](https://docs.ligus.ai/security/): What each component holds, trust boundaries per deployment shape, encryption, roles, and the 2.0 guards.
- [Threat model](https://docs.ligus.ai/security/threat-model/): Attackers, what they can and can't do, and known limitations.
- [Runbooks](https://docs.ligus.ai/security/runbooks/): Device revocation, lost phone, compromised device, offboarding, key and token rotation.

## Concepts

- [Workspaces & chats](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/workspaces/): The event-sourced workspace model, multiple workspaces, per-workspace device-local code directories, and per-chat isolated worktrees.
- [Agents (built-in vs BYO)](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/agents/): What a workspace agent is, the dispatch model, and an agent's host (this device vs a worker).
- [Headless agents & setups](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/headless-agents/): Enrolling a headless agent/worker on a remote box via the CLI.
- [Tools & permissions](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/tools-and-consent/): How tool access and file/command permissions are gated.
- [Vaults & knowledge sources](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/vaults/): Attaching knowledge to a workspace.
- [Identity & devices](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/identity/): GitHub-based identity, one member across multiple devices.
- [Security & trust](https://docs.ligus.ai/concepts/security/): The E2EE model, what the relay can and cannot see.

## Features

- [Settings](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/settings/): Every settings section — Account, Appearance, Folder & Git (per-workspace folder), Team sync, Schedules, Models & runtimes, Tools & MCP, Permissions, Updates, Diagnostics.
- [Right Rail](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/right-rail/): The tools/review/people/context panes.
- [Multi-agent collaboration](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/multi-agent/): Multiple agents in one chat and how they interact.
- [Exploring options (proposal sets)](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/proposal-sets/): Competing alternatives assessed blind by agent scouts, quorum and stop signals, and a person's decision after a pre-flight.
- [Mentions & notifications](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/mentions-and-notifications/): Addressing participants and how notifications work.
- [Agentic workflows](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/workflows/): Multi-stage agent pipelines and human-approval gates, including gate-routes-back loops. Agents author definitions as reviewable proposals; people approve, run and pause them.
- [Flow](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/flow/): Hand-off cards and context parcels, outcome-weighted routing of un-addressed work (shadow mode first) with adaptive exploration and cool-downs, review-queue backpressure, the threshold task board, careers, workspace marks, path zones, worktree reuse and the home beacon.
- [Ligus on your phone](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/phone-app/): The phone app over `ligus serve`: pairing direct or through the relay, host path policy, Face ID lock, demo mode, chats, proposal review, workflow approvals, push (off in standard builds), Match host, and what stays desktop-only.
- [Host dashboard](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/dashboard/): The dashboard `ligus serve` shows on the phone: built-in Ligus section, dashboard.toml panels, MCP tool panels, tables.
- [Scheduled agents](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/scheduling/): Recurring, cron-like agent runs.
- [Managing context](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/voice-and-slash/): /summarize, /compact, and the context planner.
- [Git integration](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/git/): The Diff canvas, worktree isolation, and applying proposals.
- [Invites & joining](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/invites/): Inviting teammates and joining a workspace.
- [Collaborators, presence & DMs](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/collaborators/): Members, presence, and direct messages.
- [Collaborative editing](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/collaboration/): Real-time collaboration behavior.
- [Onboarding](https://docs.ligus.ai/features/onboarding/): The first-run onboarding flow.

## Add-ons

- [Bring-your-own agents](https://docs.ligus.ai/addons/byo-agents/): Wiring any stdin-driven CLI as a Ligus runtime.
- [Skills](https://docs.ligus.ai/addons/skills/): Reusable instruction sets applied to agents.
- [MCP servers](https://docs.ligus.ai/addons/mcp/): Installing and enabling Model Context Protocol servers.
- [Linear & remote MCP (OAuth)](https://docs.ligus.ai/addons/linear/): Connecting OAuth-based remote MCP servers.

## Networking

- [LAN discovery](https://docs.ligus.ai/networking/lan/): Peer discovery on a local network.
- [Rendezvous relay](https://docs.ligus.ai/networking/rendezvous/): How peers find each other over the internet.
- [Self-hosting a relay](https://docs.ligus.ai/networking/self-host/): Building and running the relay, storage (Postgres or snapshot), TLS, token modes, membership, tunnel and APNs push, rate limits, monitoring, backups and upgrades.
- [TURN fallback](https://docs.ligus.ai/networking/turn/): Relayed connectivity when P2P fails.
- [Remote access for your phone](https://docs.ligus.ai/networking/remote-access/): The relay tunnel, `ligus pair`, `ligus phones`, `ligus remote`, self-hosted relays and push.

## Operations

- [Building the dist](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/build/): Building the desktop app.
- [Operations](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/operations/): Health endpoints, logs, backups and restore of data dirs, upgrades.
- [Running ligus serve as your own device](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/serve-box/): `ligus serve enroll`, host liveness, apply-on-approve, and the 1.16 sync privacy upgrade note.
- [Pricing tiers](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/pricing/) and [Tiering (open-core)](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/tiering/): The open-core model.
- [Managed service plan](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/managed-service/): The hosted option.
- [Server-side membership](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/server-side-membership/): Relay-managed team membership.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.ligus.ai/ops/troubleshooting/): Problems by symptom: sync stuck, relay 401s, phone can't connect, worker not picking up turns, plan windows, hygiene sweep.

## Reference

- [What's new](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/whats-new/): Changes since 1.15 with links.
- [CLI](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/cli/): Every `ligus` command and flag.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/env-vars/): Every `LIGUS_*` variable, its default and who reads it.
- [Serve HTTP API](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/serve-api/): Every `ligus serve` route, auth, limits and the SSE stream.
- [Settings](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/settings/): `settings.json` keys, CLI `config.toml`, and what the workspace config log carries.
- [Configuration (TOML)](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/config-toml/): The `ligus.config.toml` reference.
- [Invite payload format](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/invite-payload/): The invite/enroll payload structure.
- [Wire protocols](https://docs.ligus.ai/reference/wire-protocols/): The `/v1` relay wire contract and token format.
